newsitem.title: UK: U.K. North Sea October oil output hits 1996 high.
newsitem.headline: U.K. North Sea October oil output hits 1996 high.

text.p: U.K. North Sea oil production set a new monthly high for 1996 in October, the Aberdeen Petroleum Report said.
Field figures give a daily average of 2,608,947 barrels per day (bpd) compared with the year's previous high of 2,601,773 bpd in February.
The October total was boosted by significant monthly increases in production from Shell Expro's Brent and Enterprise's Nelson fields.
Shell Expro's Brent production grew by 10,000 bpd, while Enterprise's Nelson field production was up by 28,744 bpd.

The Aberdeen Petroleum report said this represented an 116,340 bpd rise on September's 2,492,607 bpd average, in line with the 1995 year end trend which pushed output to 2,697,351 bpd in November last year.

It said last month's total also benefited from new field production, with Conoco's Banff field returning a 25,194 bpd average from a first full month's production. Amerada's Fergus and Agip's Thelma fields also made their first significant contributions while BHP's Liverpool Bay development reached a new peak of 35,000 bpd from the Douglas field.
